target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D036) defines the fiscal year convention (52/53 weeks ending near Oct 31) and states that 2023 was a 52-week year. The 2024 filing splits this topic: D043 defines the general convention (similar to 2023 D036), while D003 specifically discusses the 2024 vs 2023 comparison (53-week vs 52-week) and the impact of the extra week. D003 contains specific comparative data not present in D043, and D043 contains the general policy definition present in D036. Both are needed to cover the fiscal year presentation topic completely.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD had $5.0 billion in unconditional purchase commitments as of December 28, 2024, primarily for wafer and substrate purchases, with $4.5 billion due in fiscal year 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address financial obligations and liquidity management, though AVGO specifically notes the impact of its fiscal calendar structure on revenue recognition, while AMD details unconditional purchase commitments for wafer and substrate purchases. AVGO highlights that its 53-week fiscal year 2024 resulted in higher net revenue due to an additional week in Q1, whereas AMD quantifies specific contractual liabilities ($5.0 billion) related to supply chain inputs. Both represent critical financial resource disclosures in Item 7, but they focus on different aspects: AVGO on revenue timing/calendar effects and AMD on future cash outflows/commitments.

sentences.text: We operate on a 52- or 53-week fiscal year ending on the Sunday closest to October 31.
Our fiscal year 2024 was a 53-week fiscal year.
As of December 28, 2024, we had unconditional purchase commitments of approximately $5.0 billion, of which $4.5 billion are in fiscal year 2025.

Our contractual obligations and purchase commitments relate primarily to our obligations to purchase wafers and substrates from third parties and future payments related to certain software and technology licenses and IP licenses.
